paragraphs.source_en: Managing Stakeholders 303 (continued) The issue is that, unless you make this clear at the outset, that new leader may assume you’re hiring them for their knowledge of process and how to define and deliver products. And, so they bring with them their views on how things should work. Even worse, they often then proceed to hire people that want to work in those ways. Note that I’m picking on Oracle here as an example, but they are certainly not the only one. There are a great many very strong people to hire from Oracle as they love to acquire companies, often very good companies, but those strong product, design, and technology people they also acquired rarely like Oracle’s culture or ways of creating product. I have seen this anti-pattern play out at every level of a company—from individual engineers all the way to CEO. It doesn’t happen overnight; it happens over years.
